note: Curated knowledge base. Source facts (title, venue, one-line summary, mechanism) are stated as the work describes itself. The alignment columns are this lab's assessment and are labelled as such in the UI. Identifiers are given where verified; where an identifier is not verified, the url is a search that always resolves.

dimensions.label: What it rewrites
dimensions.question: Which part of the harness changes when the agent learns?

dimensions.label: Learning isolated per task family
dimensions.question: Is what the agent learned kept from being applied to a task family it was not learned on?

dimensions.label: How a stored experience is matched
dimensions.question: When the agent recalls something, what decides that it applies?

dimensions.label: Degradation measured
dimensions.question: Does the work measure interference or forgetting across a changing task stream?

dimensions.label: Disjoint hold-out
dimensions.question: Is the agent graded on instances it was not trained on?

dimensions.label: Evidence kind
dimensions.question: What kind of source is this?

dimensions.label: Forgetting handled
dimensions.question: Does the work specify what is discarded or kept as memory grows?

dimensions.label: Cost of learning reported
dimensions.question: Does the work report what learning costs: memory growth, tokens, or calls?

dimensions.label: Agent scope
dimensions.question: Does the work study one agent's memory or memory shared across agents?

concepts.label: Self-improvement
concepts.gloss: The agent changes something about itself - the code, the prompt, the memory - and is judged on the result.

concepts.label: Experience replay
concepts.gloss: Past episodes are stored and replayed as guidance for a later task.

concepts.label: Reflection
concepts.gloss: The agent writes an account of what went wrong, and that text is what it uses next time.

concepts.label: Skill library
concepts.gloss: Reusable capabilities are accumulated as named, retrievable units.

concepts.label: Memory management
concepts.gloss: What the agent keeps, and how it decides what fits in its working context.

concepts.label: Prompt optimisation
concepts.gloss: The prompt or program is compiled from data and feedback rather than written by hand.

concepts.label: Verifier feedback
concepts.gloss: A checker, grader or environment decides success, and only success is learned from.

concepts.label: Continual learning
concepts.gloss: Learning over a stream that keeps changing, with interference and forgetting as the cost.

concepts.label: Catastrophic forgetting
concepts.gloss: Learning a new family overwrites what was learned for an old one.

concepts.label: Transfer
concepts.gloss: What is learned for one family is useful, or harmful, for another.

concepts.label: Harness engineering
concepts.gloss: The scaffolding around the model - tools, prompts, state - treated as the artefact under optimisation.

concepts.label: Agent-computer interface
concepts.gloss: The action space and the feedback are redesigned so the model can act well.

concepts.label: Test-time adaptation
concepts.gloss: The system adapts at inference time rather than at training time.

concepts.label: Self-refine loop
concepts.gloss: Generate, critique, revise, repeat within a single task.

concepts.label: Credit assignment
concepts.gloss: Deciding which part of a long trajectory deserves credit.

concepts.label: Memory-policy learning
concepts.gloss: The agent learns how to manage memory - what to store, retrieve, update or discard - not just what to remember. A-MEM's RL-trained memory operators and MemRL's runtime RL are the first instances.

concepts.label: Selective forgetting
concepts.gloss: Principled discarding: heat-based eviction, preemptive summarisation, redundancy pruning. Forgetting as a designed operation rather than context overflow.

concepts.label: Hierarchical memory
concepts.gloss: Memory organised in levels - segments, pages, traces - with different retention and retrieval at each level, after the OS memory hierarchy.

concepts.label: Multi-agent memory
concepts.gloss: Memory shared, routed or traced across agents: shared stores, per-role scopes, and conflict when agents remember inconsistently.

concepts.label: Experience evolution
concepts.gloss: Forward learning from the experience stream itself: each interaction updates the reusable repertoire (reasoning memory, latent memory, skill set) rather than only the current answer.

concepts.label: Memory benchmarks
concepts.gloss: Benchmarks that grade memory rather than single answers: long-horizon QA (LoCoMo, LongMemEval), incremental multi-turn intake (MemoryAgentBench-style), and agentic environment suites (ARE, GAIA).

works.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
works.summary: Interleaves reasoning traces with actions so the model plans while it acts.
works.mechanism: No learning: the same prompt drives every episode, with observations appended to the trace.

works.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
works.authors: N. Shinn, F. Cassano, E. Gopinath, K. Narasimhan, S. Yao
works.summary: On failure the agent writes a reflection into episodic memory and reuses it on the next attempt.
works.mechanism: Stores a natural-language reflection per episode; the next attempt is conditioned on it.

works.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
works.summary: A memory stream with reflection and planning gives an agent a believable, continuous life.
works.mechanism: Appends observations to a memory stream, retrieves by recency and relevance, and periodically reflects into higher-level notes.

works.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
works.summary: A Minecraft agent that acquires skills for itself and keeps them in a library.
works.mechanism: Automatic curriculum proposes goals; a skill library stores verified code; environment feedback drives iteration.

works.title: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
works.summary: Trains an agent to extract reusable insights from its own past trajectories.
works.mechanism: Successive trajectories are consolidated into natural-language insights that are prepended to later tasks.

works.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
works.summary: A generator, a critic and a refiner improve an answer in a loop, with no training.
works.mechanism: The same model critiques its own output; the feedback is consumed within the episode.

works.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
works.summary: Searches a tree of partial solutions with self-evaluation at each step.
works.mechanism: No learning across tasks: the search procedure is fixed and run per episode.

works.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
works.summary: Treats the context window as a managed resource with archival and recall memory.
works.mechanism: The agent itself decides when to page memory in and out of a fixed context.

works.title: Agent Workflow Memory
works.summary: Learns reusable workflows from past experience and applies them to new tasks.
works.mechanism: Workflows are induced from successful trajectories and retrieved for similar tasks.

works.title: Agent-Pro: Learning to Evolve via Policy-Level Reflection and Optimization
works.authors: W. Zhang, K. Tang, H. Wu, M. Wang et al.
works.summary: An agent learns expertise from interactive experience and elevates its behavioural policy.
works.mechanism: Policy-level reflection mines successful trajectories for proactive behaviours that are reused as guidance.

works.title: AgentTuning: Enabling Generalized Agent Abilities for LLMs
works.authors: A. Zeng, M. Liu, R. Lu, B. Wang et al.
works.summary: Tuning on agent trajectories generalises multi-turn tool use beyond the training tasks.
works.mechanism: Fine-tunes the model on successful trajectories; the weights, not the harness, change.

works.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
works.summary: Designing the tools and the feedback loop so an LM can actually do software engineering.
works.mechanism: The interface - commands, file viewer, lint feedback - is the contribution; the model is frozen.

works.title: ToolLLM: Facilitating Large Language Models to Master 16000+ Real-world APIs
works.summary: A tool-use dataset and training recipe for learning to call APIs.
works.mechanism: The model is trained on tool trajectories; the harness is fixed.

works.title: Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
works.summary: A coding agent proposes modifications to its own code and keeps only what measurably improves it.
works.mechanism: Archive of self-modifications, selected empirically against a held-out benchmark; nothing is kept on assertion alone.

works.title: Godel Agent: A Self-Referential Agent Framework for Recursive Self-Improvement
works.authors: X. Yin, X. Wang, L. Pan, L. Lin et al.
works.summary: An agent that rewrites its own logic, evaluated as it goes.
works.mechanism: Self-modification of the agent's own code, with evaluation gating each accepted change.

works.title: Continual Learning of Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Survey
works.authors: H. Shi, Z. Xu, H. Wang, W. Qin et al.
works.summary: Surveys the methods and the evaluation protocols used for continual learning of language models.
works.mechanism: A survey: it organises the field and compares the protocols, including catastrophic forgetting.

works.title: A Survey on Continual Learning of LLM-based Agents
works.summary: Surveys how LLM agents are evaluated under a changing task stream.
works.mechanism: A survey: it catalogues the evaluation protocols used for agent continual learning.

works.title: A Survey on Large Language Model based Autonomous Agents
works.summary: A survey of the architectures, the memory and the planning used by LLM agents.
works.mechanism: A survey: it organises the design space agents are built from.

works.title: DSPy: Declarative Self-Refining Language Model Programs
works.summary: Optimisers compile a prompt program from data and a metric, then keep the version that scores best.
works.mechanism: The prompt program is the artefact; an optimiser proposes variants and a metric selects the winner.

works.title: Letta (MemGPT) - the stateful agent server
works.summary: A server where the agent's memory blocks, tools and system prompt are the durable, editable state.
works.mechanism: Memory blocks are first-class persisted context that an operator or an agent can rewrite.

works.title: Claude Code
works.summary: A coding agent whose durable knowledge lives in CLAUDE.md files and in skills.
works.mechanism: Project instructions and reusable skills are read into context; they are written by the user, and skills can be authored as the agent works.

works.title: Cursor
works.summary: An editor agent with project rules and a memory that carries decisions between sessions.
works.mechanism: Rules and memories are durable artefacts read into every request.

works.title: LangGraph
works.summary: Graph-structured agents with a checkpointer, so a run's state is durable and resumable.
works.mechanism: The graph is the harness; the checkpointer stores state, and a store holds cross-thread memory.

works.title: OpenHands
works.summary: An open platform for software-development agents, with a runtime, a sandbox and microagents.
works.mechanism: The agent's tools, runtime and microagent configuration are the product surface.

works.title: CrewAI
works.summary: Role-based agents composed into flows, with memory and training over past runs.
works.mechanism: Flows define the workflow; memory stores prior runs and can be trained into the agents.

works.title: OpenAI Agents SDK
works.summary: Agents, handoffs, guardrails and sessions as first-class parts of the harness.
works.mechanism: The session is durable state; guardrails are deterministic checks in the loop rather than prompt text.

works.title: AutoGen
works.summary: Conversable agents that hand work to each other, with a memory layer over the conversation.
works.mechanism: The conversation protocol is the harness; memory and termination are separate components.

works.title: Building effective agents
works.summary: Where to draw the line between a workflow and an agent, and what each is good for.
works.mechanism: Guidance, not a mechanism: it argues that simple composable patterns beat opaque autonomy.

works.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
works.summary: Context is a finite budget: the write-up is about choosing what goes in it.
works.mechanism: Guidance: curating the context, compaction and just-in-time retrieval rather than training.

works.title: Don't Build Multi-Agents
works.summary: A warning that parallel sub-agents fragment context and lose the main thread.
works.mechanism: Argument, not a mechanism: it argues for a single context and a tool-first design.

works.title: The Bitter Lesson
works.summary: Methods that scale with compute beat methods that rely on human knowledge.
works.mechanism: Argument, not a mechanism: the recurring lesson that hand-built structure loses to learning.

works.title: Are Self-Evolving Agents Continual Learners?
works.authors: X. Chen, Y. Huang, Y. Xu, Z. Zhao et al.
works.summary: Tests whether agents that rewrite their own harness from task feedback actually learn continually.
works.mechanism: Nonparametric self-evolution: prompts, memory and skills are rewritten while the model weights stay frozen, over four drifting task streams.

works.title: Self-Evolving Agent Harness
works.authors: C. Wei, H. Guan, M. Zhu, K. Zhou et al.
works.summary: Formalises harness self-evolution: what may change, who proposes it, and who admits it.
works.mechanism: Separates update targets from proposal and admission mechanisms, and distinguishes interpreted state from tools, code and plugin composition.

works.title: EvoHarnessBench: Can Your Agents Keep Pace with an Evolving Harness?
works.authors: Z. Ke, V. Patil, H. Shi, Y. Li et al.
works.summary: A benchmark that puts the non-stationarity in the harness, not in the task stream.
works.mechanism: 17 multi-stage harness streams that add tools, skills and specialist agents, so the agent's own scaffolding changes under it.

works.title: Continual Learning, Not Training: Online Adaptation For Agents
works.summary: Gradient-free continual adaptation at inference time, with a memory that stores distilled guidance.
works.mechanism: A Teacher/Student pair: a persistent learning memory holds distilled experience, and the orchestration layer adjusts supervision and plan choice from it.

works.title: From Storage to Experience: A Survey on the Evolution of LLM Agent Memory Mechanisms
works.authors: J. Luo, Y. Tian, C. Cao, Z. Luo et al.
works.summary: Places agent memory on a three-stage path: storage, reflection, experience.
works.mechanism: A survey: it frames the field's memory designs as a progression rather than a catalogue.

works.title: Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
works.summary: Production memory layer with user/agent/run scoping and hybrid retrieval.
works.mechanism: Extracts salient facts per turn into scoped stores; retrieves by vector/graph hybrid at inference.

works.title: A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
works.summary: Zettelkasten-style note network whose link structure the agent evolves.
works.mechanism: Notes carry keywords and links; agentic operators create, link, update and discard them.

works.title: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
works.summary: Scales self-evolution by distilling episodes into retrievable reasoning memory.
works.mechanism: Successful trajectories are distilled into reasoning notes retrieved by query similarity on later tasks.

works.title: MemInsight: Autonomous Memory Augmentation for LLM Agents
works.summary: Autonomously augments agent memory with structured attribute summaries.
works.mechanism: Mining interaction history into augmentations that are injected alongside retrieved context.

works.title: Memory OS of AI Agent
works.summary: OS-inspired memory: segments, pages and heat-based management across dialogue.
works.mechanism: Short/mid/long-term segments with heat scoring for update and eviction; fewer calls and tokens than MemGPT/A-MEM baselines.

works.title: GAIA: a benchmark for General AI Assistants
works.summary: 466 real-world assistant tasks requiring tools, browsing and multi-step reasoning.
works.mechanism: Fixed task set with deterministic scoring; no learning component, graded on held-out tasks.

works.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
works.summary: Real GitHub issues with hidden tests; the standard agentic-coding benchmark.
works.mechanism: Repository snapshot plus fail-to-pass tests; agents are graded on instances unseen in training.

works.title: G-Memory: Tracing Hierarchical Memory for Multi-Agent Systems
works.summary: Hierarchical memory traced across agents in a multi-agent system.
works.mechanism: Per-agent memory organised in a hierarchy with cross-agent tracing and consolidation.

works.title: MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime Reinforcement Learning on Episodic Memory
works.summary: Learns the memory policy itself - how to remember - with runtime RL over episodic memory.
works.mechanism: Step-wise RL rewards memory operations (store, link, summarise, discard), including preemptive summarisation.

works.title: FLEX: Continuous Agent Evolution via Forward Learning from Experience
works.summary: Evolves the agent forward from the experience stream without waiting for failures.
works.mechanism: Each interaction updates the reusable repertoire used on later tasks.

works.title: LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
works.summary: 500 curated questions over ~500-turn histories; the harder successor to LoCoMo for memory QA.
works.mechanism: Fixed long histories with abstention-aware scoring; retrieval-only grading on unseen questions.

works.title: LoCoMo: Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents
works.summary: Multimodal long dialogues (~300 turns) graded on single/multi-hop and temporal questions.
works.mechanism: Fixed dialogues with QA probes; the retrieval benchmark every memory layer reports on.

works.title: Letta Memory Benchmark (Letta Leaderboard)
works.summary: Apples-to-apples memory benchmark: fixed framework and tools, varying the model.
works.mechanism: Runs LoCoMo-style tasks through one agent scaffold so scores compare models, not harnesses.

works.title: ARE: Scaling Up Agent Environments and Evaluations (Gaia2)
works.summary: Scalable dynamic agent environments and evaluations beyond static task sets.
works.mechanism: Procedurally scaled environments with held-out evaluation episodes.

works.title: AutoGPT: build, deploy, and manage continuous AI agents
works.summary: The 2023 autonomous-agent reference: goal loop with vector-store memory and tool use.
works.mechanism: Persistent vector memory plus self-prompted planning loop; community plugin ecosystem.
